strategy.summary: Family-owned German iron foundry (founded 1936, financially sound) supplying our HN impellers under a framework agreement: HN 200 shared with a cheaper Polish source, HN 250 single source. It has a long record of settling below its ask and of pricing HN 200 below our should-cost to keep volume. The owner personally invoked a past price hold and expects partnership in return. Delivery reliability has collapsed, concentrated on the single-source HN 250, and quality runs above the peer median. We pay late habitually, which weakens our partnership standing. The new HX volute casing RFQ, in competition with a Turkish foundry, is the big prize and our main bundling lever. There is little price room on the existing parts; the room lies in the new part and in non-price terms. The renewal and price-notice window is about to close. Evidence on its capacity and on the cause of the delivery slump is thin.
strategy.decision_maker: The owner (family firm). He visited personally and frames the relationship as reciprocal partnership. The new inside-sales contact handles day-to-day correspondence but likely has no pricing authority, so expect escalation to the owner.

persona.style: Relational and proud, keeps score of past favours. Concedes on price to keep volume, but expects recognition and reciprocity.
other_traits: financially sound, can afford to walk (we are a small share of its turnover)
history of accepting below-full-cost prices to keep volume
new inside-sales contact with limited authority
possible capacity strain behind the delivery decline (unconfirmed)

needs.detail: Acknowledgement of the price hold it gave us in 2022, and partnership treatment in return.
Wants to keep or grow its share. It has accepted below-cost prices for HN 200 volume and wants the HX volute award.
Wants to recover full cost on HN 200 and pass through steel and labour increases. It has asked for an increase every year recently.
No cash stress, but our habitual late payment is an irritant. Paying on time or slightly faster is a cheap goodwill gift.
A longer commitment and binding volume give it continuity, especially as HN 250 volume dips.

constraints.detail: The HN 200 price is below our bottom-up should-cost for its plant, so further cuts are unsustainable.
HN 250 is single-sourced here (we own the tooling), and its delivery is the worst.
Prices are fixed per calendar year. A change needs 90 days' notice before year-end. The contract auto-renews unless notice is given within 90 days.
Possible capacity strain: it misses its own confirmed dates, and the heavy HX casing would add load. This is unconfirmed.

The new HX volume is the reciprocity the owner asks for. Use it as a bundle for fair terms across all parts.
Grounds a fair target for the new casing, which is where the real price room is.
A factual, checkable slump against the contract target. Frame it as a joint problem to fix and use it to justify ppm/OTD commitments, not as an attack.
ppm above the peer median: a fresh fact to support quality terms or resist an increase.
The checkable power-cost fall offsets part of a claimed driver increase on HN 200.

The iron castings PPI rose only modestly, which caps any justified increase below its likely ask.
Anchors the current HN 200 price as the base for any change.
Recurring defects on the single-source part; supports a ppm commitment on HN 250.
The contract's OTD target and complaint fee support asking for a performance commitment.
Alternative approved sources exist for HN 200. Mention calmly and only if it pushes hard; never as a threat.

trades.why: It has no cash need, so do not spend money on faster payment. Instead commit to paying on time, which fixes our weak spot and honours the partnership.
A longer commitment gives continuity to a volume-seeking family firm. 24 months captures the value.
Binding HN 200 volume (forecast rising) is what it trades price for; commit within our need.
Quality and delivery are slipping. A tight ppm target protects us on the single-source HN 250 and costs it little if it fixes root causes.
The current fee costs it almost nothing. Test a higher fee as a trade item rather than conceding it.
Accept its own lead time; possible capacity strain means short lead times would be priced steeply.
Steel is rising, so a steel clause carries upside risk for us. Offer one only if it insists, with a fair base and no deadband.
If an increase is unavoidable, a later start at a slightly higher price may cost us less.

price_view.reasoning: HN 200 already sells below our should-cost, and a recurring note says it accepted below full cost to keep volume. Its checkable drivers (steel, labour up; power down) net to a modest increase, capped by the iron castings PPI. HN 250 is roughly at cost by weight, with falling volume and single source, so it has no room downward and a modest increase is plausible. The HX volute is new and competitive, with a should-cost anchor; the real room is there, though our estimate is only accurate to about five percent. The rival's lower HN 200 price reflects a different cost base, not margin at Velkenreith.

do: Thank the owner explicitly for the past price hold and frame offers as partnership and reciprocity.
Address substance to the owner even when writing to inside sales.
Raise delivery and quality as a shared problem to solve, with facts.
Bundle the existing parts and the HX award into one coherent partnership offer.
Bring our own verified figures instead of questions.
dont: Never threaten resourcing or termination, or set deadlines.
Do not cite the Polish rival's actual order price.
Do not demand further cuts on HN 200 below cost.
Do not complain about performance while ignoring our own late payment.
Do not ask open questions about its cost calculation.

traps: Pushing HN 200 further below cost: margin charge, walk-away risk and possibly further delivery deprioritisation.
Citing the Kalwisz order price reveals a rival's price and insults a firm that sees itself as the quality source.
Long-run index peaks (steel or power since 2022) are not checkable and cost trust; use only the 12-month changes.
Copper, electronics and alloy-surcharge news are irrelevant to cast iron; do not use them.
Overplaying single-source fears on HN 250 or signalling urgency weakens us.
Asking for long payment terms plus a price cut ignores its request for partnership.
Awarding HX volume without checking capacity could worsen HN delivery.
Letting the renewal and price-notice window lapse unnoticed.
Pushing past a declared final offer.
strategy.writer_notes: Open every negotiation by recognising the long relationship and the past price hold, and position the new HX casing as the reciprocity the owner asked for. Keep the existing impellers near their current price through volume, contract length and our commitment to pay on time, rather than by squeezing. Seek real savings on the new casing, anchored on our should-cost. Use delivery and quality records as joint improvement topics that justify ppm and on-time commitments, held back as fresh facts for later rounds. If the supplier claims cost increases, answer with the checkable power decline and the modest castings price trend. Never threaten; stay warm and factual. Note where evidence is thin: capacity and the root cause of late deliveries are unknown.

findings.text: Part 310030 (Impeller HN 200): current price EUR 34.26 sits about 4.8% BELOW our bottom-up should-cost of EUR 35.98 for its own plant (no margin). The ±5% error band covers this, so at best it is at break-even. Notes on four renewals say it accepted below full cost to keep the volume. There is no real price room here. Pushing further risks the margin charge, and the supplier may drop the 70% quota.

Part 310030 has a structural price gap to its rival. Odlewnia Kalwisz supplies the same part at EUR 30.14, 12% below Velkenreith and about 16% below our should-cost. In the Sept 2025 benchmark Kalwisz quoted 32.90 and Pfaffenreuth 36.80, while Velkenreith quoted 37.90, still won the award and then settled at 34.26. The Polish price is not explained by Velkenreith's German cost base. It is leverage on share (70/30 quota, tooling owned by us), not proof that Velkenreith has margin.

Cost drivers over 12 months modestly favour the supplier. Using the 310030 weights: labour +2.7% (≈+0.88%), steel/ferro-alloys +6.5% (≈+1.50%) and power -3.7% (≈-0.34%) net to about +2.0% on price. Part 310031 nets about +1.9%. Long-run views argue the other way: steel is -6.3% since its 36-month peak and -26.7% since 2022, and power is -43.5% since 2022. These long-run comparisons are not checkable, so they serve only as context. The iron castings PPI is +1.8% year on year, which is a fair ceiling for any increase. The copper (+48%) and electronic boards (+41%) news is irrelevant to cast iron.

Part 310031 (Impeller HN 250) has no should-cost. Its price of EUR 54.42 has been flat since 2024 (-3.9% since 2023). Scaling by weight from 310030 (35.98 for 6.5 kg ≈ 5.5 EUR/kg against 54.42/9.8 kg ≈ 5.55 EUR/kg) suggests it is also near full cost, but this is only a rough estimate. Our position here is weaker: Velkenreith is the single source, and the volume outlook is falling (4870 vs 5160 pieces).

Part 310070 (Volute casing HX 80-200, new part) has a should-cost of EUR 194.18 on a German cost base, without margin. With a margin of 5-10% a fair price would be about EUR 204-214, before DAP freight for 44 kg. The RFQ is open, and Tarsevi (TR) is a competitor here. This is where the economic room lies, but our estimate's confidence is only about 5%.
The supplier is financially sound: equity ratio 38.5%, credit index 239 and stable. We are only about 1.4% of its turnover, so a below-cost squeeze is more likely to make it walk away than concede.

findings.text: Decision-maker is the owner of a family firm (founded 1936). He visited in person on 2026-07-19 and framed the relationship as reciprocal: in 2022 they held the old price for a quarter, and he 'expects partnership in return'. He will read our e-mails personally and will be sensitive to tone, threats and any lack of recognition. Day-to-day contact moved to a new inside-sales colleague, who probably has limited authority, so pricing decisions likely go up to the owner.

The company is financially sound and not under stress: turnover EUR 34.2 M, 240 staff, equity ratio 38.5%, credit index stable at 239, VDA 6.3 grade A, ISO 9001/14001/50001. We are only about 1.4% of its turnover. It can afford to walk away, so pressure without reciprocity is risky.

It repeatedly accepted prices below full cost to keep volume. The part 310030 price sits about 4.8% under should-cost. It settles well below its opening asks, by about 2.2-2.3 pp. It values volume and continuity, which signals that the margin on our business is thin and that the owner's 'partnership' remark may precede a margin-recovery push.

Our payment behaviour is a sensitivity. We pay 90.4% of invoices late, 4.8 days late on average and up to 15 days, on a contractual 45 days net. This undercuts our partnership claim. Paying on time or faster is a cheap gift that matches what the owner wants.

Its performance is weakening, which gives us legitimate leverage. On-time delivery is 74.5% against a 95% target, down from 87.5% a year earlier. Quality is 734 ppm against a peer median of 457. One 8D on part 310031 is still open.

New business is in play: an RFQ for volute casing HX 80-200 (part 310070), 4200 pc/yr, SOP March 2027, in competition with Tarsevi Döküm (TR). This is the volume and recognition the owner seeks and can be traded against fair terms. The contract renewal notice deadline is 2026-10-02, which gives us a credible exit.
The evidence is thin overall: no news and no cost letters from the supplier, and only one meeting note.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070120 covers only HN 200 and HN 250. Prices are fixed per calendar year (clause 3.1). Payment is 45 days net against our 60-day standard. Delivery is FCA with a 49-day lead time. Quality terms are a 95% OTD target and EUR 150 per complaint. The contract runs to 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless one side gives 90 days' notice. That notice deadline is 2026-10-02, days away: if we do nothing, the contract rolls into 2027.

Any 2027 price change needs written notice by about 2026-10-02 (90 days before year end). If no notice arrives, 2026 prices stay fixed. The volute casing HX 80-200 (part:310070) is outside the contract and is in an open RFQ with Tarsevi.

History: the supplier settles about 2.2-2.3 pp below its ask, every year, on both parts. HN 200 went from asking +2.6% to settling -1.4% in 2025-12. HN 250 has been held flat at 0% for two years despite asks of +2-3.2%. Four HN 200 events are noted 'accepted below full cost to keep the volume'. Should-cost says HN 200 sells 4.8% below cost, so further cuts are unsustainable and raise a margin-health risk.

Dependency is asymmetric by part:
- HN 200: we own the tooling and split it 70/30 with Kalwisz, which is cheaper (EUR 30.14 actual, 32.90 quoted). Pfaffenreuth is qualified but dearer (36.80).
- HN 250: the supplier is our 100% single source, with no other approved source, though we own the tooling.
- Relative weight: we are about 1.4% of its turnover, and it is financially sound.

Performance is weak against the contract: OTD 74.5% against a 95% target (down from 87.5%), and 734 ppm against a peer median of 457. This gives us a contractual lever (clause 6.1) but not a termination case. The owner invokes his 2022 sacrifice and expects partnership in return.

findings.text: Delivery has deteriorated sharply: rolling OTD vs requested date fell from 90.5% (2024Q3) and 87.5% (2025Q3) to 74.5% (2026Q3), against a 95% target and a 84.6% peer median. OTD against its own confirmed dates fell from 97.6% to 78.2%, so it is missing its own promises, not only ours. The scorecard dropped from class A green to B amber in 2026Q2.

The lateness is concentrated on part:310031 (HN 250, single source). In the last 12 months only 63% of its receipts were on time against the requested date, 33% were late and the worst was 25 days late. Part:310030 runs at 85.7% on time. Confirmations later than requested occurred on 11 lines. Recent POs were confirmed on the requested date, so the slippage shows up at shipment rather than at confirmation.

Quality is stable but above peers: 734 ppm rolling (707 a year earlier) against a 457 ppm peer median. All complaints except one are supplier-caused. Part:310031 runs at 883 ppm over the last 12 months against 573 ppm on part:310030. Coating and surface defects recur. 8D discipline is good (0 overdue). Two QNs are still open without a D8: qn:20004982 (not supplier-caused) and qn:20005013. Recharges are only EUR 150 per complaint, so defects cost the supplier little.

On part:310030 Velkenreith is the better-quality source. Its 573 ppm compares with 4433 ppm at sup:70140, which also needs rush lines. Velkenreith's 70% share is therefore partly earned, despite sup:70140 being about 12% cheaper.

Volume outlook differs by part:
- Part:310030 rises to 8530 pcs forecast against 7472 ordered (+14%), which is attractive to it.
- Part:310031 falls to 4870 against 5160 (-5.6%), which supports its case for a higher price.
- The new part:310070 (SOP 2027-03, 2490 pcs in the first 7 months; the RFQ states 4200 pcs per year at 44 kg) is a large prize. It could more than double our spend with Velkenreith, and gives us bundling leverage.

Prices have only fallen: part:310030 from 36.82 to 34.26 (-7%) and part:310031 from 56.62 to 54.42 (-3.9%). Should-cost for part:310030 is 35.98, meaning it sells below cost. Under a stabilise logic, a further cut on part:310030 is weak and risks margin charges.

arguments.text: HN 200 is already below our full cost. Hollerau's own bottom-up estimate of our plant puts it at EUR 35.98 with no margin. We sell at EUR 34.26 and have cut it in each of the last three renewals. Any further cut is out of the question, and we need a step toward cost recovery.

Our checkable cost drivers have risen. Basic iron and steel is up 6.5% in 12 months (and 7.3% since January), with a weight of about 0.23. Labour is up 2.7%, with a weight of about 0.3. HN 250 has been held flat for three years, at 0% in both 2025 and 2026, despite asks of +2% and +3.2%. A modest increase of about 2.5-3% is justified.
Partnership track record. We kept supplying at the old price for a quarter in 2022, and our owner raised this personally. We settled below our ask in every renewal. We now expect reciprocity.

Quality advantage over the alternative. On HN 200 our ppm over the last 12 months is 573, against 4,433 for Kalwisz. The cheaper Polish price comes with more than seven times the defects and 8 rush lines. Pfaffenreuth's benchmark quote of EUR 36.8 was above our current price.
Hollerau pays late. 90.4% of invoices are paid late, by 5.9 days on average. That is effectively a longer payment term than the contractual 45 days, and it costs us interest.

We are a financially sound, certified German partner close to Hollerau for the new HX casing: equity ratio 38.5%, VDA 6.3 grade A, ISO 9001, 14001 and 50001. Logistics risk and lead-time risk are lower than with a Turkish source.

weak_points: Delivery performance has collapsed. On-time delivery is 74.5% (78.2% against our own confirmed dates), and HN 250 is at 63% with up to 25 days late. The scorecard has dropped to class B / amber.
Quality ppm of about 734-820 is above the peer median. There are recurring coating and surface defects, and an open complaint qn:20005013 from 2026-09.
Power prices have fallen: -3.7% in 12 months and -43% against 2022. The iron castings PPI is only +1.8%, which caps a credible increase.
HN 250 volume forecast is dropping by 5.6%, which weakens us. Hollerau owns the tooling and could move it to Pfaffenreuth, which is already qualified.
Our 2025 RFQ quote of EUR 37.9 was well above the price we later accepted, so our quoted prices look inflated.
Capacity: we are missing our own confirmed dates, and the heavy HX casing adds load. We have no convincing explanation yet.
The price-notice window under clause 3.1 is about 2026-10-02. If we miss it, prices stay fixed for 2027.
wants: HX volute award: we would accept a sharp price close to cost on HX, and hold HN prices, in exchange for the award and a multi-year contract.
A 2-3 year framework extension with binding annual volumes on HN 200/250. In return we would freeze prices or accept a smaller increase.
A higher HN 200 quota (from 70% toward 100%) in exchange for holding price.
On-time payment, or 30 days, as a substitute for part of the price increase.
An index clause on steel (PPI-C241) instead of a fixed price, in exchange for a lower base price.
A delivery improvement plan in exchange for not being pushed further on price.
red_lines: No price cut on HN 200 below EUR 34.26; it is already below cost.
No HX price below our own full cost of about EUR 190-195 without margin cover elsewhere.
No penalty or chargeback escalation tied to delivery while price is held below cost.
No longer payment terms than 45 days without price compensation.
red_team.opening: Thank you for the HX invitation; we want to grow with Hollerau. Ahead of the year-end notice deadline, we propose +3.5% on HN 250 and +4.5% on HN 200, pointing to steel up 6.5%, labour up 2.7%, Hollerau's own should-cost of EUR 35.98, and three years of concessions and the 2022 price hold. We acknowledge the delivery slippage and present a recovery plan. We signal openly that a joint package of an HX award, a 3-year extension and binding volumes would let us moderate the HN increases substantially.

rebuttals.answer: Our aim is to keep this part stable, not to squeeze it. A step toward recovery has to be earned through the whole relationship, though. The volume on this part is rising, and that growth spreads your fixed costs across more pieces. We would rather reward you with a longer commitment and binding volume than with a price increase on a part where deliveries are currently missing target.

It is true that steel and labour have risen over the last twelve months, and we accept those index figures. Taken at their weight in the part, though, they explain only part of the increase you ask for. Power is a real share of a foundry's cost, and it has fallen over the same period. Producer prices for iron castings as a whole rose only modestly. Netting the drivers you cite against the power fall supports a clearly smaller adjustment than the one requested. We are willing to discuss that properly calculated figure, ideally tied to a longer agreement rather than a clause.

We remember the quarter in which you held the old price, and we are genuinely grateful for it. That is exactly why we want to answer it with something substantial. We have invited you to quote for the new HX volute casing, a significant new volume. We also offer a longer agreement and committed volumes on the impellers. Partnership works both ways, and we would ask the same of you on delivery reliability, where we currently fall short of what the agreement sets out.

Across both impellers, however, your rolling ppm is above the peer median and slightly worse than a year ago. The benchmark round also showed that more than one approved source can supply this part. We value your quality and want to protect it, ideally through a joint ppm commitment.

You are right, and we will not argue it: we have too often paid a few days late. We will commit to paying on the contractual due date as part of this agreement. That is a fair point to fix on our side. Fixing it is the correction of our own slip, not a reason for a higher price, and it gives you back the interest you mention.

Your financial strength, certifications and proximity are real advantages, and we will weigh them fairly in the HX comparison on total cost, including freight and lead time. Two things weigh on the other side. The price has to stand against our own cost estimate for this casing. And we need confidence that the extra load will not further affect impeller deliveries, which have slipped against your own confirmed dates. A clear capacity plan from you would make your offer much stronger.

press: Could you share how you would add the HX casing alongside the impellers without affecting the confirmed dates you give us today?
We would like to agree a ppm target together, focused on the recurring coating and surface defects, so that quality becomes a shared strength again.
For a fair view of costs, we suggest netting the steel and labour rises against the fall in power prices and the modest rise in iron castings prices.
A longer agreement with committed impeller volumes and our on-time payment could give both sides the stability we each are looking for.
